workspace.brief: The 90-day software trial is ending. A sales campaign starts next week and the vendor’s offer expires at 5 p.m. Advise Mariam, the owner: sign, reserve, negotiate, or decline. This is a fictional classroom business simulation.

prompts: What is the setup payment due today? (AED)
What is the daily licence fee? (AED)
How many working days does setup take?
How many days does a reservation hold the price?
The company wants mean dispatch lateness below how many minutes?
How many days did the vendor include?
What kind of days did the vendor select?
What daily saving does the vendor report? (AED)

references.title: Statistical reference
references.sourceLabel: Mizan Market case pack · Reference tables, page 4 · 10 November 2026

sections.title: Choose and interpret the test
sections.body: Use the 5% significance level chosen before seeing the reports. These are general methods and reference tables, not worked answers.
bullets: For a population mean with unknown population SD, use t = (sample mean − null benchmark) / (sample SD / √n), with n − 1 degrees of freedom, under the stated sampling assumptions.
For a population mean with known population SD, use z = (sample mean − null benchmark) / (known population SD / √n).
Choose the tail from the claim before looking at the result: greater than uses the upper tail, less than uses the lower tail, and different from uses both tails.
A p-value is a tail probability under the null model and assumptions. It is not the probability that the null is true. Failing to reject does not prove the null.
Critical-value tables may bound a p-value rather than give an exact value. State a justified range or compare with the chosen significance level instead of inventing precision.

sections.title: Student’s t
sections.body: Entries are critical values for the upper-tail probabilities in the headings. Use symmetry for the lower tail. Select the degrees of freedom, then compare the signed statistic with the critical value in the appropriate tail.

table.caption: Student’s t critical values from the case pack

sections.title: Standard normal
sections.body: Entries give the probability to the left of a standard normal value. The row gives units and tenths; the column gives hundredths. For a negative value, use symmetry: Φ(−z) = 1 − Φ(z). Upper-tail probability is 1 − Φ(z); lower-tail probability is Φ(z). For a two-sided test, use twice the smaller tail.

table.caption: Standard normal cumulative probabilities from the case pack

competitionRules: There are 15 independent scored questions, worth 2 points each: Round 1 has 6 points, Round 2 has 12, and Round 3 has 12, for 30 in total.
The team leader saves the team’s answers. The latest saved answers count when each round closes; automatic scores and ranks then update. An unsaved round earns zero points.

Each verified member of a top-scoring team with a positive total receives one percentage point of the course grade. Equal positive top totals share the full winning-team bonus; an all-zero competition has no bonus winner.
There are no speed points or instructor-assigned marks. The business action, class vote, role notes, findings and reflection do not affect the score.
The three scored rounds sit inside a longer decision process: first recommendation, company analysis, audit choice and report review, final recommendation, then the common Round 3 exercise.
All spending is fictional classroom cash. Team decisions are recorded once and retained across role and leadership handoffs.
workspace.bonusRule: Each team starts with 1 bonus point. The winning team collects 0.5 from every other team; each other team keeps 0.5. Tied positive top teams split the collected points equally. With no positive top score, each team keeps 1. Each verified member earns the team’s bonus in course percentage points.

packet.subject: Finance brief · What can we afford?
packet.summary: Separate cash due today from the full contract cost.

messages.title: Cash position
messages.body: We have AED 10,000 available today. Setup, audit fees and any reservation payment use this cash. Daily software fees come from the regular business budget.

messages.title: Original offer
messages.body: The term is 180 operating days. Software costs AED 240 per operating day. The full AED 7,200 setup fee is due today.

packet.task: Calculate the mean daily gross saving required to cover the entire original contract. Share the calculation and the cash needed today.

packet.subject: Operations chat · Five days to set up

messages.title: Campaign readiness
messages.body: Staff group orders by hand and often work overtime. Setup takes five working days. Signing today allows us to start before next week’s campaign.

messages.title: Reservation trade-off
messages.body: AED 1,000 holds the quoted price for seven days. The fee is not returned. Waiting seven days misses the first campaign week.

packet.task: Explain the trade-off between starting on time and getting stronger evidence. Do not invent a monetary cost for the delay.

packet.subject: Vendor email · Offer closes at 5 p.m.
packet.summary: A sales assertion is not the team’s conclusion.

messages.title: Sales follow-up
messages.body: “Average savings were AED 340 a day. That easily beats a licence price of AED 240. The pilot already proves the business case.”

messages.title: Decision mandate
messages.body: We need a decision today. Tell me what the numbers support and what risks are left. You can sign, reserve the price, ask for different terms, or decline. The seller must agree to changes.

packet.task: Separate the vendor’s claim from established evidence. Record a first recommendation and the assumption that could change it.

packet.subject: Company report · Labour savings
packet.summary: Use gross savings before software and setup fees.

messages.title: Independent sample of operating days
messages.body: The company report uses 16 operating days from the 90-day trial. Mean daily gross savings are AED 300. The sample SD is AED 80; the population SD is unknown.

messages.title: Decision question
messages.body: Tell me whether the evidence supports mean savings above the amount needed to cover the full contract, not merely the daily licence fee.

packet.task: Set up the savings test at the preselected 5% significance level. Share the signed statistic, reference distribution and interpretation.

packet.subject: Audit firm quote · Choose before opening
packet.summary: Purchasing information reduces cash available for setup.

messages.title: Today’s audit options
messages.body: Savings audit: AED 1,800, checking 64 unused trial days. Dispatch audit: AED 1,800, checking 100 other orders. Both: AED 3,600. Neither: AED 0.

messages.title: Records selected in advance
messages.body: The samples were chosen before your decision and do not overlap the first company samples. The fee buys a check and its report today. Choose one plan before seeing the results.

packet.task: Recommend one audit plan and explain what information is worth the cash. The leader commits the team’s plan once.
